_comment: CReserveTransfer output scripts produced by verusd 1.2.17-2 on VRSCTEST, 2026-07-29, via sendcurrency with returntxtemplate=true so nothing was spent. crates/verus-tx/src/convert.rs reproduces every one byte-for-byte.

_layout.script: PUSH(master: version3, EVAL_NONE, 1-of-1, dest=RESERVE_TRANSFER_ADDRESS) OP_CHECKCRYPTOCONDITION PUSH(params: version3, EVAL_RESERVE_TRANSFER=8, 1-of-1, same dest, vdata=[CReserveTransfer]) OP_DROP
_layout.payload: tokenOutput(version=1 || sourceCurrency(20) || varint(amount)) || varint(flags) || feeCurrency(20) || varint(fee) || destination || destCurrency(20) || [secondReserve(20) if RESERVE_TO_RESERVE]
_layout.destination: varint(type) || compactSize(len) || bytes || [if type&64: compactSize(count), then per aux compactSize(len) || (varint(type) || compactSize(len) || bytes)]
_layout._note: amounts and flags use the Satoshi VARINT (7 bits per byte, high bit continues, minus-one adjustment), NOT compact size; the crate's existing cc::var_int is exactly this

reserve_transfer_address._why_constant: It is NOT derived from the system or destination currency. Verified by observing the same address in every template, and by balance: it has received 84,248,804 VRSC on mainnet and 3,678,445 VRSCTEST on testnet. It is a protocol constant on both chains.
reserve_transfer_address._important: The output pays THIS address, not the recipient. The recipient is inside the payload.

vectors.name: burn
vectors._note: no auxiliary destination: type byte 2 rather than 66. destCurrency is the currency being burned.

vectors.name: reserve to reserve via a fractional
vectors._note: TWO trailing currency ids: destCurrency is the via fractional, then secondReserve is the final target.

_proven_on_chain._what: A conversion built, signed and broadcast entirely by this SDK through api.verustest.net: 1.0 VRSCTEST into shylock. The node estimated 0.99443551 and exactly 0.99443551 shylock arrived at RJKGReAJv5qUZJvhVeaGB8exY1ku58D1n7 two blocks later.
_proven_on_chain._not_covered: preconvert (only valid before a currency launches), mint (needs the currency's controlling identity), and cross-chain export (needs a second system). Those remain unbuilt.
